name: Aurelis
subtitle: The City Above the Clouds
author: Luminati
description: A 128 × 128 city of white marble and gold on islands floating over a sea of clouds: the Cathedral of the Dawn Halo on the Sanctum Isle with its beam and halos, the Court of Radiance between two rills that fall into the void, the Grand Viaduct from the Arrival Terrace, the Gardens of Aster, the Athenaeum and its observatory, the Crystal Islets, the Terraces of Dawn and the Lantern Quay — nine viaducts, floating islets, crystals, rune circles and camera vistas. Generated by tools/make-aurelis.mjs.

objects.name: Seraphel
dialogue: Welcome to Aurelis, the City Above the Clouds. You are standing on the Arrival Dais; the sigil under your feet is the one that brought you up.
Walk north between the {Obelisks of Morning} and take the {Grand Viaduct} to the Sanctum Isle. Mind the edges: the clouds are softer than they look, and a great deal farther down.
objects.title: Herald of Arrivals

objects.name: Caelan
dialogue: The Obelisks of Morning catch the first light before anything else in Aurelis. We stand guard between them. It is mostly a matter of standing.
objects.title: Warden of the Gate

textKeys.title: 46C39A0312D3D89AB177335DD48247A9
dialogue: F348D0CFEB19AE82A89962A74BAD6268

objects.name: Oriel
dialogue: Walk the middle of the viaduct. The wind likes the rails.
West over the little viaduct are the Terraces of Dawn; east, the Lantern Quay. Both are lovely. Only one sells honey.
objects.title: Warden of the Gate

objects.name: Bram
dialogue: First time up? Me too. The lift-sigil spun me round nine times and set me down facing the wrong way.
Down in the Groundlands they say Aurelis is held up by wishes. Up here they say it is held up by maths. I am keeping an open mind.
EB3E755F5B6B8BE88ED26DF04EB47299
FBCA3C3BB0EE51A4F884F1B15339D70F

objects.name: Pip
dialogue: My brother says if you drop a pebble off the Arrival Terrace it lands on a goat in the Groundlands. I have dropped forty. That is a lot of goats.

objects.name: Liora
dialogue: The rotunda is where we say goodbye to people going down. It is also where we say hello to them coming back, so on balance it is a cheerful sort of place.
84A381CAC5418CE6C9735CBDB6DE5378

objects.name: Aldwin
dialogue: From here you can watch the clouds pass under the city like a slow white river. I have been watching for forty years. It has not once run dry.
objects.title: Keeper of the South Lookout

objects.name: Aldous
dialogue: Halfway. From here the cathedral looks as if it stands on the clouds. It does not, of course. It stands on us.

objects.name: Lumen
dialogue: Every lute in Aurelis is tuned to the {Keelstone}, the great crystal that hangs under the Sanctum Isle. Lay your ear on the court floor and you will hear it hum.
objects.title: Bard of the Court

objects.name: Isolde
dialogue: Four steps to the Cathedral of the Dawn Halo, each of them polished by nine hundred years of slippers. Go up; the Luminar likes visitors.
Under the court turns the {Keelsigil}, the great circle that holds the Sanctum Isle aloft. Lean over the south rail and you can see it glow.
objects.title: Keeper of the Grand Stair

textKeys.title: 09C704C025364E0E41EA5AF53834C342
dialogue: 2E9B1B8CFAE7E3E7C325096331FD8D6F

objects.name: Bastien
dialogue: I guard the stair. The stair has never once tried to leave, so I think I am doing well.
objects.title: Court Guard

objects.name: Marisol
dialogue: West over the rill and the Garden Viaduct lie the Gardens of Aster; east, the Athenaeum and its observatory. The Sanctum is the middle of everything, and it knows it.
objects.title: Court Guard

objects.name: Celestine
dialogue: They say the Court of Radiance was laid out by starlight: every gold star in the floor lies under the star it is named for.
AF2652D3BFCA9BDC33751A395C0B856B

objects.name: Dorian
dialogue: I come every morning to watch the crystal turn. It has never turned the same way twice. I have written it all down, in eleven volumes.
A8601A3109810BDE97DEDAC3BCBA85DD

objects.name: Wren
dialogue: My kite got away! It is blue, with a gold star on it. The wind took it west, toward the Gardens of Aster.

objects.name: Halcyon
dialogue: When I was a boy the Dawn Halo turned the other way. Either that, or I spent my boyhood standing on my head. One of the two.

objects.name: Vesper
dialogue: The rills run from under the cathedral terrace and off the edge of the island. Nobody knows where the water comes from, and nobody minds, which is the Aurelian way.

objects.name: Solenne
dialogue: Welcome to the Cathedral of the Dawn Halo. Nine hundred years ago the first halo was lit over its spire, and the Sanctum rose with the sun.
The beam above us is the {Lumen}, the city's heart-light. If it ever dims, every bell in Aurelis will ring. So far that has only happened when the bell-ringers dozed off.
objects.title: High Luminar of the Dawn Halo

objects.name: Maelis
dialogue: I polish the gold. All of it: every finial, every halo seam. By the time I reach the last one, the first needs doing again.
objects.title: Acolyte

objects.name: Peregrine
dialogue: The bells hang in the two belltowers. We ring them for the dawn, for weddings, and whenever the Luminar mislays her spectacles.
objects.title: Bell-ringer

objects.name: Ignatius
dialogue: I came all the way up from the Groundlands to see the Halo turn. It was worth every step. Well, every step of the lift.
objects.title: Pilgrim

objects.name: Sorrel
dialogue: Cypresses grow straight up here. With nothing to lean on, they simply reach.
objects.title: Gardener

textKeys.title: 7852639281865868A84504CE9798B786
dialogue: F0AC082528E1310EEE974C57ACF43A5D

objects.name: Ondine
dialogue: I paint the clouds under the city. By the time I finish one, it has turned into another, so I have painted a great many clouds and never the same one twice.
objects.title: Painter

objects.name: Elowen
dialogue: Welcome to the Gardens of Aster. Something blue is caught on the halo over the pond: a kite, I think, with a gold star on it.
The halo will not come down, and I will not go up, so there it stays until the wind changes its mind.
objects.title: Head Gardener of Aster

textKeys.title: 22BEB15A28C9CADF0EC31C5E107E48F4
dialogue: 61CFCEB3F602E677549D122DBAA50E6C

objects.name: Corvin
dialogue: I am writing a poem about the pond. The pond reflects the sky, and the sky reflects nothing at all, so the poem is going to be very short.
objects.title: Poet

textKeys.title: A30E0DC5C0E5896B2E58A4B303D7729A
dialogue: 8DF3F01BB4287AF9DEC119719FC5E89D

objects.name: Linnea
dialogue: We were married under the halo by the pond. It turned the whole time. Very romantic, and very dizzying.

objects.name: Evander
dialogue: She said yes before the halo had gone round twice. I have counted every turn since.

objects.name: Tamsin
dialogue: The birds know me. They are only sparrows, but they are very well-mannered sparrows, and they never take more than their share of the crumbs.

objects.name: Juniper
dialogue: Elowen says I may go on the flower terraces as long as I do not step on anything purple. Nothing up there is purple. I checked very carefully.
D7E4F8A558827457F9AEE8A98B79D0FB

objects.name: Cassia
dialogue: The Hall of Charts holds every map ever drawn of the islands. Every island drifts a hand's width a year, so every map is wrong. We keep them anyway: they are beautifully wrong.
The Keelstone under the Sanctum hums a perfect A. Every instrument in the city is tuned to it, which is why our music is so agreeable.
objects.title: Archivist of the Athenaeum

objects.name: Noor
dialogue: North, past the clouds, stand the spires of Thessaly, our sister city. On clear nights we signal each other with mirrors. They mostly signal back: what?
objects.title: Astronomer of the Athenaeum

objects.name: Phineas
dialogue: I am studying why the islands float. Current theory: very politely.

objects.name: Yselle
dialogue: There are four thousand books in the Lumen Library, and I have read the one about cats seven times.
5D5857C1CC131B3ADEC215427E7CD4E8

objects.name: Rowan
dialogue: The crystals hum if you are quiet. That one hums flat. Do not tell it.
F794B5CAFF31F12123EFFDDDC25CC087

objects.name: Vale
dialogue: This obelisk keeps the Gardens of Aster aloft. I tune it every morning with a silver fork and a great deal of patience.
objects.title: Crystal-tuner

objects.name: Halden
dialogue: The eastern obelisk sings a little sharper than the western. We call that character.
Look north through the {Gate of the North}. On a clear day you can see the spires of Thessaly over the clouds.
objects.title: Crystal-tuner

textKeys.title: ACCA6DC99ABA43847801AFD2DB22CF8C
dialogue: E87BFF835EAEAB5074A54FA0CFF59C04

objects.name: Lady Aurelia
dialogue: My family has watched the dawn from this terrace for eleven generations. The view has not changed. The neighbours have.
DB2FDC436E6F97F5E08484DE0DCE74AC

objects.name: Captain Ewan
dialogue: I have flown a skiff to every island you can see from here, and to three you cannot.
The trick is never to look down. The other trick is never to look up. Look straight ahead and hum something cheerful.
objects.title: Skiff Captain, retired

objects.name: Sabine
dialogue: We are called the Terraces of Dawn because the sun reaches us first. We are very smug about it.
ADDE010B505FDE7C2EDAFC5E06F4485A

objects.name: Tobin
dialogue: Our cat sleeps on the warmest step in the whole city. It moves one step at a time with the sun.

objects.name: Marchetta
dialogue: Cloudsilk! Spun from the morning mist off the east rim. Light as a sigh, warm as a rumour.
objects.title: Cloudsilk Weaver

objects.name: Bertrand
dialogue: Starglass, fresh from the Crystal Islets. Hold it to your eye and the clouds go clear. Mostly.
CE0ECD5A5AB499F611952FA8F280440D

objects.name: Old Hettie
dialogue: Honey from the lower world, carried up by skiff. Bees will not fly this high, the cowards.
7822AC6376E7175C9DDC7D6CA8CC5F51

objects.name: Quillon
dialogue: Maps! Every one of them slightly wrong, and every one of them wonderfully cheap. The Athenaeum throws them out; I give them a second chance.

objects.name: Warden Brisk
dialogue: Mind the skiffs. There are none today. Mind the absence of skiffs.
objects.title: Quay Warden

objects.name: Ottoline
dialogue: The mist comes up thickest here at dawn. The weaver pays me for it in honey, and I pay the honey-sellers in compliments.
objects.title: Mist-gatherer
